channel.title: Inventory on Best of AI
channel.description: Recent content in Inventory on Best of AI

item.title: Afresh
item.description:
The system looks at sales history, shelf life, and promotions and recommends order quantities. Store teams review suggestions on a tablet. Grocers use it to cut spoilage on perishable items.

It is an enterprise service for grocery chains.

Blue Yonder and Relex offer broader retail planning. Afresh suits grocery managers focused on fresh departments.

item.title: Manhattan Associates
item.description:
Its warehouse management system directs picking, packing, and inventory placement. Order management coordinates stores, warehouses, and online orders. AI agents and optimization features help with labor planning and slotting.

It is an enterprise product, and implementations take months.

Blue Yonder and Oracle are alternatives. Manhattan Associates suits warehouse managers at large operations.

item.title: Sortly
item.description:
Users add items with photos, tag them with barcodes or QR codes, and scan to update counts. Low-stock alerts prompt reordering. Reports show stock by folder and value.

A free plan covers basic use, and paid plans add more items and users.

inFlow and Zoho Inventory are alternatives. Sortly suits inventory managers at small operations.

item.title: Zonos
item.description:
Merchants and brokers use it to classify products into tariff codes, estimate duties and taxes at checkout, and create paperwork. AI helps match product descriptions to HS codes. APIs plug into shops and carriers.

Classification still benefits from review for unusual goods.

Avalara and Flexport offer related services. Zonos suits customs brokers and cross-border sellers.

item.title: Freightos
item.description:
Freightos brings quoting and booking for international freight online. Shippers and forwarders enter details about a shipment and receive rates from carriers and forwarders, then book and manage the shipment on the platform. This replaces emailing multiple providers for quotes.

WebCargo is the air cargo side, used by forwarders to get rates and book space with airlines. Freightos also publishes the Freightos Baltic Index, a benchmark for container spot rates that is often cited in news about shipping costs. Its data helps businesses understand market conditions.

item.title: o9 Solutions
item.description:
o9 targets the planning process in big supply chains. Instead of separate systems for forecasting, inventory, production, and finance, it builds one connected model of the business, called the Enterprise Knowledge Graph, so a change in demand updates the supply plan and the financial outlook. Planners can run what-if scenarios to compare options before choosing.

Machine learning forecasts demand using sales history, promotions, weather, and other signals, and the platform recommends actions such as shifting inventory or changing production. Generative AI features let planners ask questions in natural language and summarize risks. Customers include consumer goods, retail, and manufacturing companies with complex networks.

item.title: FourKites
item.description:
FourKites is a supply chain visibility platform. It collects location and status data from carriers, telematics devices, and ocean and air sources, and shows shippers where each load is. Predictive estimates of arrival time account for traffic, weather, and dwell time at facilities, which are more accurate than static schedules.

Alerts warn teams of delays so they can reroute or notify customers. Yard and dock scheduling tools coordinate appointments, and analytics help identify problem carriers or lanes. AI agents handle tasks like checking on late shipments and communicating with carriers.

item.title: project44
item.description:
project44 is a supply chain visibility platform. It gathers location and status data from trucks, rail, ocean, and air carriers, merges it into one view, and shows shippers where each shipment is. Predictive ETAs account for traffic, weather, and port conditions.

Alerts flag delays early, so teams can reroute or notify customers. The platform also offers tools for appointment scheduling, drayage, and analytics on carrier performance, and AI features automate routine tracking tasks and communication.

item.title: Zycus
item.description:
Zycus is a source-to-pay suite. Companies manage supplier onboarding, sourcing events, contracts, purchase orders, and invoice processing in one platform, giving procurement teams visibility and control over spend.

AI agents assist with the work. They read contracts to extract terms, detect anomalies in pricing or invoices, suggest suppliers, and draft communications. Analytics show savings and compliance.

Zycus is sold to large enterprises on subscription. Alternatives include Coupa, SAP Ariba, Jaggaer, Ivalua, and GEP. Zycus suits procurement teams at large organizations.

item.title: Flexport
item.description:
Flexport is a freight forwarder with a software platform. Companies that import and export goods book shipments, track containers, manage documents, and handle customs through a single interface, instead of coordinating by email with many parties. It also offers financing, warehousing, and trade services.

Technology handles repetitive work. AI reads shipping documents, checks customs data for errors, and predicts delays based on port, carrier, and weather information. An assistant answers questions about shipment status and helps with classification of goods. Data from many shipments feeds analytics on cost and performance.

item.title: Blue Yonder
item.description: Blue Yonder helps companies plan and run their supply chains. Demand forecasting predicts what customers will buy, inventory planning decides how much stock to hold and where, and transportation and warehouse systems manage how goods move. Retailers, manufacturers, and logistics providers use it to balance supply and demand, reduce stockouts and excess inventory, and respond to disruptions. The company grew from JDA Software and acquired an AI startup that gave it its name.

item.title: Llamasoft
item.description:
Llamasoft helped companies answer strategic supply chain questions. Where should factories and warehouses be placed? How would costs change if a port closes or demand shifts? Its software builds a digital model of a supply network, then uses optimization and simulation to test alternatives and recommend the best configuration, balancing cost, service levels, and risk. Large manufacturers, retailers, and consumer goods companies used it for network design and planning.

Coupa acquired Llamasoft and folded it into its business spend management platform, so customers can connect supply chain decisions with procurement and spend data. The technology continues under Coupa branding, with capabilities such as network optimization, inventory and sourcing analysis, and demand sensing, supported by machine learning and a digital twin of the supply chain.

item.title: Oracle SCM
item.description:
Oracle SCM Cloud brings the functions of a supply chain together in one cloud application suite. It covers planning demand and supply, buying from suppliers, managing inventory and warehouses, running manufacturing, handling orders and fulfillment, and moving goods through transportation and global trade, with product lifecycle management for design data. Because it shares data with Oracle’s finance and HR applications, companies can connect supply chain decisions to financial outcomes.

AI and analytics support the suite. Machine learning improves demand forecasts and supply plans, predictive models flag delays and quality risks, and generative AI assistants help users find information and complete tasks. Oracle has been adding AI agents that can handle routine actions across processes. The suite is delivered in the cloud and updated regularly.

item.title: SAP Ariba
item.description:
SAP Ariba helps large organizations buy what they need in an organized way. Procurement teams use it to find and evaluate suppliers, run sourcing events, manage contracts, process purchase orders and invoices, and monitor supplier risk. The Ariba Network connects buyers and suppliers electronically, so orders and invoices flow between systems without manual entry.

AI is being added to reduce manual work. SAP’s assistant, Joule, can help users search for information, draft sourcing documents, and answer questions about spend, and features analyze contracts, recommend suppliers, and flag unusual transactions. Integration with SAP’s ERP and other systems provides a connected view of purchasing, and spend analytics reveal savings opportunities.

item.title: Coupa
item.description:
Coupa gives companies control over what they spend. Employees request purchases through approved channels, procurement manages suppliers and contracts, and accounts payable processes invoices and payments. Having it in one system improves visibility and helps enforce policy.

The company’s distinctive asset is aggregated data. With permission, Coupa analyzes anonymized spend across its customer base to benchmark prices, identify supplier risk, and recommend savings. AI features help with spend classification, contract review, and answering questions about spending, and supplier networks connect buyers with vendors.

item.title: Kinaxis
item.description:
Kinaxis helps large manufacturers and retailers plan and respond. Its platform brings demand, supply, inventory, and capacity into one model that updates together, rather than in separate steps, so planners can test the effect of a disruption or a decision in minutes.

Planners run what-if scenarios, see the impact on service and cost, and collaborate across functions. Machine learning improves demand sensing and supply risk detection, and newer AI agents help summarize issues and recommend actions. Customers include companies in high tech, life sciences, automotive, and consumer goods.
